os.p: When a library breaks in production, I report it upstream with a reproducer instead of quietly working around it.
os.1: PDFs stopped rendering on iPhone 15 Pro after the 5.4 upgrade while iPhone 11 still worked. I isolated the device-specific regression.
os.2: ContextMenu items could no longer be swapped at right-click time after the processedItems internals changed.
os.3: Dialog drag broke when the cursor crossed into the body, so the handle disappeared mid-drag.
os.4: Proposed server-side lazy loading for Dropdown virtual scroll (page index and size on scroll-to-end).

ng.alt: Nawa Captcha website: "the self-hosted, accessible puzzle CAPTCHA" with a live drag-the-piece puzzle, an open-source reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha and Turnstile alternative.
ng.p: An open-source puzzle CAPTCHA that runs on your own server: no third-party tracking and no data leaving your app. 3D-styled puzzles with optional sound, an audio challenge for blind users and 6 themes. Widgets for React, Vue, Svelte, Angular and plain HTML, with verification on Node.js or ASP.NET Core.
ng.h1: The client is never trusted: puzzles render on the server and the answer is sealed with AES-256-GCM
ng.h2: Short-lived, single-use, HMAC-signed pass tokens verified on your own backend, like siteverify without the third party
ng.h3: Everyone can pass it: mouse, touch, full keyboard, a text alternative and an audio challenge for blind and screen-reader users, in Arabic and English with RTL
na.alt: 5min Refresh API: OpenAPI docs page and architecture diagram

na.h1: Cookie sessions done right: argon2id, HttpOnly + Partitioned cookies, session rotation, CSRF tokens and strict CORS
na.h2: Offline-first sync that merges conflict-free (max stars, best time) and never awards XP twice, with ETags and anti-cheat checks
na.h3: Zod schemas drive validation and OpenAPI 3.1, with 89 tests at 94% coverage and a real Postgres run in CI
